script.base: JAX is a 1.5-point home favorite in a 43.5 game, implied 22.5-21.0, so the base is a one-score, moderate-pace game that is still live in the fourth. Both lead backs stay in their two-game roles (Etienne 30 carries/214 yards, Chubb 25/103) without a clock-kill spike. Houston blitzes 32% and Lawrence has been better versus the blitz (EPA/db +0.34 vs +0.03 with no blitz), so JAX can stay on schedule through the air even if rush efficiency dips. JAX blitzes 33% and Stroud has been poor versus the blitz (EPA/db -0.36 vs +0.07), so Houston's deep air (Collins 123 air yards, only 77 yards) is the part of the script most likely to stall.
script.flip1: JAX gets up by two scores early, runs the clock, and Etienne's carries climb toward 20-plus while Houston abandons the run. Chubb's rush line dies, Stroud is forced into the blitz, and late JAX skill snaps get managed. That flip is what beats an Etienne rush under.
script.flip2: Houston leads and JAX plays from behind, so Etienne's carries dry up and Lawrence's air yards (Thomas already 19 targets/258 air yards for only 60 yards) become the offense. A slog or unsaved weather would also drag both implied totals under the low-20s and kill yardage overs. Etienne under survives this flip.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report only: HOU CB Jaylin Smith Out (hamstring) is a depth corner, a small rotation loss for Houston's secondary and a mild, non-specific boost to JAX receivers (Thomas, Hunter, Brown), not a HOU offensive gainer. No HOU skill player is listed out, so Chubb, Collins, Schultz, Hutchinson, Marks and Stroud are treated as available. JAX G Wyatt Milum Out (knee) and G Ezra Cleveland Questionable (ankle) thin the interior. That lowers rushing efficiency for Etienne (30/214, 7.13 YPC) and Tuten (11/53) and should raise pressure on Lawrence, which normally lifts quick throws to Strange (9 targets/76 yards), Etienne (6 targets) and Hunter and cuts clean deep shots to Thomas. Offset in the pack: Lawrence's EPA/db versus blitz is +0.34, so pressure has not been killing this pass game in two games. If Cleveland plays, the efficiency hit shrinks. No same-position skill sleeper; the outs are a corner and a guard. Unknown whether Milum played in weeks 1-2, so the OL note is a this-week absence, not a proven role change.

Collins 25 and 52 on 123 air yards, inefficient and split around 38.5. Thomas 11 and 49 on 258 air yards, efficiency that has not repeated upward. Brown 52 and 57 is the only JAX receiver stuck on a high number from both sides. Schultz 28 and 29, Hutchinson 30 and 29, both glued to their stand-in lines. Strange 59 and 17. edge_players.must_be_true: Etienne stays the lead back around 14-18 carries, Milum is inactive, the game stays inside one score so he does not get a 22-carry clock-kill, and he does not repeat a 40-plus yard explosive.
edge_players.kills_it: Another 143-yard home-run game, or JAX leads big and he grinds past 107 on volume even at a normal YPC, or Cleveland plays and the interior holds up, or Houston's 4.58 YPC on two games is a small-sample mirage.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the under lost because Etienne ripped another 140. Houston has already allowed 4.58 YPC and 5 runs of 10+ in two games, so they do not tackle in space, and a home-run back's 143-yard game can be the mode rather than the outlier. Milum is one guard; Cleveland was only questionable and may have played, and it is not in the pack that Milum even played in the 214-yard fortnight. JAX is the favorite, and a two-score lead turns 15 carries into 22, which clears 107.5 at a modest 5.0 YPC. The 107.5 figure is not a stale market price to beat; it is a median stand-in, and right-skew means one explosive still cashes the over. That counter is why this is a lean, not a strong, and why it stays flagged.
slip_story: Standalone competitive-game efficiency lean, not a shootout stack and not a favorite-runs-the-clock stack. It wins with a close or Houston-led script (flip 2) and loses with flip 1. Do not pair it with JAX team-total overs, Etienne rush overs, or a total over. No second prop survived the pre-mortem, so there is no 3-4 leg slip. No TD legs.
